title: Quadrats & transects
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: When should I use a quadrat instead of a transect?
How accurate are these methods for estimating animal populations?
Can I use these methods to estimate the density of different species?

explain.say: Today we are learning about estimating populations in an area.
First we will look at random sampling using quadrats.
A quadrat is a square frame used to estimate density.
Next we will explore transects for measuring along a line.
We will then learn how to make estimates from samples taken.
Finally we will look at mark-recapture for animal populations.

faq.q: How big should my quadrat be for best results?
faq.a: The size should be appropriate for the area and the organism you are studying. Using a consistent size is most important.
asks: Is there an ideal size for sampling?

faq.q: Does the area I sample affect my final estimate?
faq.a: Yes, the sample area must be representative of the whole habitat. You need to sample different parts of the habitat.
asks: How do I ensure my sample is fair?

faq.q: What is the difference between quadrat and transect?
faq.a: A quadrat measures density over a small, defined area. A transect measures changes along a long, straight line.
asks: When do I use a line versus a square?
What is the difference between the two tools?

faq.q: What does 'density' mean in this context?
faq.a: Density is the number of individuals found per unit area, like individuals per square meter.
asks: What is the unit for density?

faq.q: Why do I need to mark the animals in mark-recapture?
faq.a: Marking allows you to identify the same individual later when you recapture it. This helps you estimate the total group size.
asks: What is the purpose of marking?

facts: Quadrats are used to estimate the abundance and distribution of plants.
Transects are useful for measuring changes in species composition across a gradient.
Mark-recapture estimates population size based on the proportion of marked individuals.
Random sampling helps reduce bias by ensuring all parts of the habitat are considered.

quiz.say: To find the density of grass in a field, which tool is most appropriate?
quiz.why: A quadrat is designed specifically to measure the number of organisms within a fixed, small area.

wrong.0: Mark-recapture is used for counting mobile animals, not stationary plants.
wrong.1: A numberline is used to show values changing over a continuous scale.
wrong.3: A transect measures changes along a line, not the density within a fixed patch.

quiz.say: If you catch 10 rabbits, mark them, and then catch 20 rabbits, with 3 marked ones, what is the best estimate of the total rabbit population?
quiz.why: The ratio of marked to total in the second sample estimates the ratio in the whole population.

wrong.0: This incorrectly multiplies the two sample sizes together.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the marked proportion is 3 out of 10.
wrong.3: This only uses the size of the second sample, ignoring the marked proportion.

quiz.why: A transect allows you to plot how a factor, like light or species type, changes systematically from one end to the other.

wrong.0: That is the function of a quadrat.
wrong.1: That is the purpose of mark-recapture.
wrong.2: While it measures distance, its purpose is ecological change, not just length.
